answer: Prefix-diverse trellis rooting: a new identity must hang from three sponsors on distinct network prefixes, each with three epochs of tenure and at most one edge per epoch. The registry keeps the trellis acyclic and demands a willow proof from every edge, re-signed each epoch against a fresh beacon; an edge whose two ends answer in lockstep snaps and slashes its sponsor bond. A k-clone farm inside one prefix supplies no diverse edge, and the admission deposit follows a spiral where the n-th identity sharing that prefix posts 2^n times base, so marginal cost grows faster than k.
